APPROVED_OPERATIONAL_REQUIREMENTS: native Linux side-effect-free read/refresh and drift reconciliation
state publication only after successful mutation and retry after failure
scoped ownership/deletion across the ten documented resource types

APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.OBJECTIVE: Complete the ten-resource ansibleops Terraform provider as a coherent managed-resource lifecycle/reconciliation system.

STATE_MODEL.terraform_state: Terraform Core sole durable state authority

root_cause_clusters.RC1_STATE_IDENTITY: Identity/applied state can derive from mutable plan data rather than stable external keys and the last successful transition.
root_cause_clusters.RC2_REFRESH_RECONCILIATION: Read can reuse stale state or mutation helpers instead of side-effect-free native observation.
root_cause_clusters.RC3_UPDATE_TRANSACTION: Update can advance state before Ansible mutation succeeds, breaking retry/recovery semantics.
root_cause_clusters.RC4_DELETE_FAILURE: Delete can complete too early or remove beyond the owned external object.
root_cause_clusters.RC5_RUNNER_COMMAND: Runner argv/process/timeout/cancellation/temp-file handling can violate safe terminal-outcome semantics.
root_cause_clusters.RC6_NORMALIZATION_IDEMPOTENCY: Desired and observed canonical forms can differ for unordered/defaulted values, creating false diffs.

defects.observable_failure: Create can publish empty stable id.
Mutable mode or symlink target can change identity.
Observed values can disappear after provider restart.
Copy destination digest is not restart-stable.
Unchanged object can churn identity/state in a fresh process.
External directory deletion may not be detected.
External mode drift can echo prior state.
Symlink retargeting may not surface as drift.
Destination content drift may not refresh.
User shell or supplementary-group drift may not refresh.
Read/refresh can invoke ansible-playbook.
Update can publish planned values before mutation succeeds.
Failed update can leave state claiming new desired values.
Retry after failed update can be skipped.
source_digest change may not execute/publish exactly once.
Named line update can append or replay instead of replace once.
Delete can clear management before teardown result.
Failed deletion can appear completed.
Deleting one named entry can remove a sibling-managed entry.
User destroy can violate remove_home_on_destroy.
Shell metacharacters may be interpreted.
Paths with spaces may split incorrectly.
Nonzero ansible exit may be treated as success.
Timeout/cancellation may not terminate and fail reliably.
Temporary playbooks may leak on terminal paths.
Equivalent template vars can produce unstable payloads.
Equivalent mode/owner/group representations can compare unequal.
Omitted cron fields and explicit wildcards can normalize differently.
